items.title: Myra Menville Interview, 1958-05-07, 09
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...Celestan kept a group fairly well together... You had nowhere to get them... [INTERVIEWEE] (implied context of discussing New Orleans bands)

ctx.x: Well, uh, is that true in New Orleans? I mean, the, the normal small, say, three to, to eight pieces, the usual seven piece, six, six, seven piece, real, as good as jazz bands. Were they used, did the use of those tend to fall off during the, during the 20s of doing a duty?

They didn't play at all. Yeah, they had a hell of a time, and gave, finding a band to engage. There were one or two that continued, uh, um, Celestan kept a group fairly well together, although they didn't play very often. They were available. Uh, who else besides Celestan? There were two or three other Negro bands that were available, but, uh, you had nowhere to get them, and you had to go hunting for them. Now, there were small restaurants and, uh, places like Marmaloo's out at the lake there. Have you ever been…
But you said that, listening to these bands, you'd hang up for parties, almost die out completely for a while. And by what period would that be?
